title: Sweep-exclusion test never makes the taken-over clock due — the claimed 'belt and braces' due-SELECT guard is unpinned
evidence:
+  // A7: the cadence SELECT never returns a taken-over row, even when the
+  // clock is due.
+  let assert Ok(returned) =
+    rc_sql.sweep_due_reference_calls(db, "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z", 50)
+  // The employer row is still queued + due, so exactly ONE row comes back
+  // (the taken-over landlord row is excluded).
+  list.length(returned.rows) |> should.equal(1)

(+ from take_over_queued_row_stops_the_cadence_and_audits_test:
+  row_field(db, call_id, "next_attempt_at") |> should.equal(Some("")))
detail: Take-over clears next_attempt_at, so the excluded row is not due regardless of any taken_over_at guard in sweep_due_reference_calls. 'Even when the clock is due' is never exercised; removing the production guard would not fail this test.
recommended_fix: After do_take_over, re-arm the clock (UPDATE next_attempt_at = now() - interval '1 minute') on the taken-over row, then assert the due-SELECT still returns only the employer row.

title: Detail-payload negative control is vacuous: no diff hunk establishes the fixture ever contains the sentinel literal, so a leaked form_token passes
evidence:
+  // RC4.3 note: the referee's CONTACT snapshot now legitimately rides the
+  // payload (the §7.7 take-over chips + §8.3 edit prefill need it) — the
+  // negative control moved to a still-internal marker (form_token is never
+  // selected by the detail read).
+  string.contains(body, "form_token_internal_sentinel") |> should.be_false
detail: The replaced control checked a real DB value (larry@example.com); the new one checks a literal string this diff never introduces into any fixture. If form_token were selected with a real token, the check still passes. Only a leak of this exact literal fails it.
recommended_fix: Assert the key instead: string.contains(body, "\"form_token\"") |> should.be_false — or set the fixture's form_token to the sentinel literal so the value check actually bites.

title: co_nudge_bounce_stands_down_test does not isolate the W3 kind-exclusion: the stale-match rule alone produces the asserted stand-down
evidence:
+  let assert Ok(_) =
+    pog.query(
+      "UPDATE reference_call
+       SET status = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status,
+           attempts = '[{\"at\":\"2026-08-01T08:00:00Z\",...,\"detail\":\"co_nudge_send_1\",\"kind\":\"co_nudge\"}]'::jsonb
+       WHERE id = $1::uuid",
+    )
+  ...
+  webhooks.apply_delivery_failure(... send_ref: "co_nudge_send_1", ...)
+  row_field(db, call_id, "status") |> should.equal(Some("queued"))
+  count_audit(db, "reference_call_correction_exhausted") |> should.equal(0)
detail: The co-nudge entry's at (2026-08-01) predates corrected_at (now() at test runtime), so the r1 W3 stale rule (pre-correction send → stand down) yields the asserted outcome even if the kind-tagged exclusion were removed from the find.
recommended_fix: Make the co-nudge entry post-correction (now()-relative 'at') so only the kind-exclusion can stand the bounce down, and keep the referee-send control as the positive.

title: RC4.3 columns verified against the migration FILE only, not the DDL surface the older columns are checked against
evidence:
+  let assert Ok(rc43_contents) =
+    simplifile.read(
+      "../supabase/migrations/20260812140000_reference_call_corrected_name.sql",
+    )
...
+  list_each_true(
+    [
+      "corrected_name",
+      "corrected_at",
+    ],
+    fn(c) { string.contains(rc43_contents, c) },
+  )
detail: draft_answers/taken_over_at/corrected_email/corrected_phone are asserted against read_ddl() contents, but corrected_name/corrected_at only against the standalone migration file. A migration that exists but is unapplied/drifted from the DDL still passes this test.
recommended_fix: Also assert "corrected_name" and "corrected_at" against `contents` (the same surface as the earlier columns) once the migration is reflected in read_ddl().
